chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ilyas, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Jahm. He said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather. He said: I heard Abu Talib narrating from Abd al-Muttalib, who said:

Once, while I was sleeping in the Hijr of Isma'il, I saw a dream that frightened me. So I went to the soothsayer of Quraysh, wearing a cloak of silk, and my hair flowing to my shoulders. When she looked at me, she recognized the change on my face, and she sat upright. At that time, I was the chief of my people. She said: What has happened to the chief of the Arabs that his colour has changed? Has something terrible from the vicissitudes of time troubled him? So I said to her: Indeed, this past night while I was sleeping in the Hijr, I saw as though a tree had sprung from my back. Its top had reached the heavens, and its branches had reached the East and the West. I saw a light shining from it seventy times greater than the light of the sun. I saw the Arabs and the non-Arabs prostrating before it, and every day it increased in greatness and in light.

I saw a group from Quraysh wanting to cut it down, but whenever they approached it, a young man — the most beautiful of people in face and the cleanest in clothing — would seize them, break their backs, and gouge out their eyes. I raised my hand to reach for one of its branches, but the young man shouted at me: 'Stop! You have no share of it.' I said: 'For whom is the share when the tree is from me?' He said: 'The share is for those who have clung to it, and you shall return to it.'

Then I noticed the colour of the soothsayer had changed. She said: 'If you have told the truth, a descendant of yours shall rule the East and the West and shall be raised as a prophet among the people.' Thereupon my worry lifted from me. Abu Talib used to narrate this hadith while the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had already appeared, saying: 'The tree was, by God, Abu al-Qasim the Trustworthy (al-Amin).'

key_terms.أبو القاسم الأمين: Abu'l-Qasim the Trustworthy — the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), known by his kunya (teknonym) and epithet
key_terms.الحجر: The Hijr — the semi-circular enclosure adjacent to the Kaaba, attributed to Ismail; a sacred space
key_terms.الشجرة: The tree — a symbol of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) in this prophetic dream
key_terms.الكاهنة: Female soothsayer/diviner — pre-Islamic Arabian oracle who claimed to foretell the future
key_terms.حدثان الدهر: Vicissitudes of time — the changing fortunes and trials of life

ai.seo_question: What is the dream of Abd al-Muttalib about the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a long chain back to Abd al-Muttalib (the Prophet's grandfather), recounts a prophetic dream that foreshadowed the emergence of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). Abd al-Muttalib saw a cosmic tree growing from his back reaching heaven and spreading to East and West — a symbol of universal prophethood. The soothsayer of Quraysh confirmed that a descendant of his would rule the world and be sent as a prophet. Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, later identified the tree as the Prophet himself when he appeared. The account reflects pre-Islamic awareness of the coming of the final Prophet, preserved through Shia transmission in al-Amali al-Saduq.
